Subject: Latency & accuracy drift after v4.2-quant rollout

Hi Lauren,

We pushed the v4.2-quant model yesterday afternoon to 100% and started seeing issues overnight. Over the last 10 hours: p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.3s, overall throughput is down ~35%, and we're seeing a small but meaningful uptick in 5xxs (from 0.4% -> 3.2%). More concerning: our evaluation set shows a subtle accuracy drift on ranking and entity extraction (failure cases attached).

Attached: hawkview_traces_0721.zip (API traces + sample requests). Example request ids: req_b3f9, req_c22a, req_d4e1.

Can you confirm whether something changed in quantization profile or default batching? This is impacting our peak hours (US east). We need an ETA for mitigation — the product team is escalating to our CTO.

Thanks,
Dana Park
Head of Platform, HawkView

Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency & accuracy drift after v4.2-quant rollout — HawkView urgent

Quick update from infra profiling of the attached traces: latency regressions correlate with a switch to the "int4_aggressive" quant profile in v4.2. Two findings:
- Kernel fallback: on our NVidia A100 fleet, the int4_aggressive path is hitting a slower fallback kernel for some attention shapes (sequence lengths ~1k). That increases per-token op time and amplifies p95.
- KV growth: v4.2 introduced an extra BOS token normalization that increases KV cache size for some request patterns, causing extra memory churn and occasional backpressure + 5xx spikes at peak concurrency.

Immediate mitigation that I recommend and can execute now:
1) Switch quant profile for HawkView's production tag from int4_aggressive -> int8_mixed (expected latency improvement, small cost increase).
2) Temporarily reduce max_batch size for their route from 32 -> 16 to avoid backpressure while KV churn is investigated.

If they accept, I can push both changes within 20 minutes. I'll attach the diff of the quant profile to this thread.

Attachments: diff_quant_profiles.json

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Jul 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: HawkView — remediation steps and exec summary (action requested)

Dana / HawkView team — thank you for surfacing this quickly and for the traces. We executed a conservative mitigation over the last 24h and wanted to summarize:

What we changed (completed):
- Switched HawkView production tag from v4.2-quant (int4_aggressive) -> v4.2-quant (int8_mixed) at 11:10 PDT on 2028-07-21.
- Reduced max_batch for HawkView inference route from 32 -> 16 during peak hours (11:15–15:00 PDT window).
- Prepared rollback plan to v4.1 (stable) which can be enacted in <15 minutes if you prefer.

Observed impact:
- p95 improved from ~1.3s -> ~270ms within the first hour after the quant flip.
- 5xx rate dropped back to baseline (0.5%).
- We do still see a small delta in ranking scores on a handful of requests; Model Ops has flagged 12 evaluation cases for a focused quality fix.

Next steps (we propose):
1) Joint postmortem call (60 minutes) to review root cause and long-term fix for KV normalization + kernel selection. Please propose times.
2) We will run a controlled canary of the fully stable v4.1 baseline against v4.2-quant with int8_mixed for 24h and share evaluation metrics.
3) Redwood will prepare an executive brief and, if you prefer, apply a credit for the incident window — Marissa will coordinate credits and CS follow-up.

Attachments: exec_brief_hawkview_0722.pdf

Please confirm whether you want us to proceed with a full rollback to v4.1 or continue on the int8_mixed path while we complete the canary. If you want the rollback, we will schedule it immediately.

Thanks again for the partnership — we recognize the impact of production regressions and are treating this as priority #1.

Best regards,
